input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# Serving-stack crypto module audit and FIPS remediation plan

## Description

Resolve the unknowns that gate FIPS 140-3 remediation of the model serving stack: produce a complete inventory of the cryptographic libraries linked into every serving-stack image, classify each as validated or non-validated, and determine the remediation approach and build-attestation source for each affected image. The findings feed the per-surface remediation work and form the module-inventory component of the compliance evidence package.

## Scope

- Enumerate all serving-stack images in scope: KServe control-plane and data-plane components, Platform Operator images, and the serving data plane model-server runtime images (vLLM, OpenVINO, Caikit-class runtimes).
- For each image, inventory the linked cryptographic libraries and modules, and classify each as validated or non-validated against the applicable cryptographic-module validation program, recording the classification source.
- For each image containing non-validated crypto, document a remediation approach (rebuild against validated modules available in the supported base images, version change, or library replacement) with rationale and risk.
- Identify, per image, the build pipeline that will produce the attestations required for the compliance evidence package; explicitly flag any gaps.
- Deliver the findings as a structured module inventory and remediation plan that the compliance evidence package can consume without rework.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every serving-stack image in scope is enumerated, and every linked cryptographic library is classified as validated or non-validated with the classification source recorded — no unclassified linkage remains.
2. Every image classified as containing non-validated crypto has a documented remediation approach with rationale and a risk note.
3. The build-attestation source for every in-scope image is identified, or an explicit gap is recorded for follow-up.
4. The module inventory is delivered in a structured form directly consumable by the compliance evidence package.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, partial): produces the module inventory that is a required component of the compliance evidence package.
- Enables HLR-1 (P0): determines the remediation scope and per-image approach for all serving-stack images.

# FIPS crypto remediation of KServe component images

## Description

Make every KServe component image run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in the inference request path. This epic also authors and verifies the FIPS regression gating check that covers KServe image builds.

## Scope

- Apply the remediation approach determined by the serving-stack crypto audit to each KServe component image identified as linking non-validated crypto (rebuild against validated modules, version changes, or library replacement, as documented in the audit's remediation plan).
- Verify the remediated images on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster: the inference request path (InferenceService deployment through endpoint serving) exercises only validated crypto.
- Author and verify the FIPS regression gating check covering KServe image builds: the check fails any KServe build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.
- Update the module inventory entries for the remediated KServe images to their post-remediation state, for consumption by the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A post-remediation scan of every KServe component image in scope shows no non-validated cryptographic library in the request path.
2. The remediated images build green in the component build pipeline.
3. The remediated images are verified to serve inference requests correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster.
4. The FIPS regression gating check is active in the KServe build pipeline and demonstrably fails a build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage (verified against a known-bad case) while passing the remediated builds.
5. The module inventory entries for all remediated KServe images reflect the post-remediation state.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): KServe component images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules, with no non-validated crypto in the request path.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the CI FIPS regression check covering KServe builds is authored and verified here — it spans the same build surfaces and remediated images as the HLR-1 work, so it is not separately schedulable as its own epic.

# FIPS crypto remediation of serving data plane runtime images

## Description

Make every serving data plane model-server runtime image (vLLM, OpenVINO, Caikit-class runtimes) run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in the inference request path. This epic also authors and verifies the FIPS regression gating check that covers serving runtime image builds.

## Scope

- Apply the remediation approach determined by the serving-stack crypto audit to each serving data plane runtime image identified as linking non-validated crypto (rebuild against validated modules, version changes, or library replacement, as documented in the audit's remediation plan).
- Verify the remediated runtime images on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster: model serving through the data plane exercises only validated crypto.
- Author and verify the FIPS regression gating check covering serving runtime image builds: the check fails any runtime build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.
- Update the module inventory entries for the remediated runtime images to their post-remediation state, for consumption by the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A post-remediation scan of every serving data plane runtime image in scope shows no non-validated cryptographic library in the request path.
2. The remediated images build green in the component build pipeline.
3. The remediated runtime images are verified to serve inference requests correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster.
4. The FIPS regression gating check is active in the serving runtime build pipeline and demonstrably fails a build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage (verified against a known-bad case) while passing the remediated builds.
5. The module inventory entries for all remediated runtime images reflect the post-remediation state.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): serving data plane runtime images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules, with no non-validated crypto in the request path.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the CI FIPS regression check covering serving runtime builds is authored and verified here — it spans the same build surfaces and remediated images as the HLR-1 work, so it is not separately schedulable as its own epic.

# FIPS compliance evidence package assembly and submission

## Description

Assemble the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and FIPS-mode test results — and submit it through the security review board to the external accredited certification laboratory.

## Scope

- Collect the post-remediation module inventory produced by the serving-stack crypto audit.
- Collect build attestations for every in-scope serving-stack image from the build pipeline identified for it (KServe components, Platform Operator, and serving data plane runtimes).
- Collect the FIPS-mode verification results from the remediated images' cluster verification.
- Assemble the package and validate it internally: every module-inventory entry is backed by attestations and test results; any gap is explicitly listed rather than silently missing.
- Submit the package through the security review board process at the defined milestones to the external certification laboratory, and track it through triage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The evidence package contains the complete post-remediation module inventory, build attestations for every in-scope serving-stack image, and the FIPS-mode test results.
2. The package is internally validated: every module-inventory entry has corresponding attestations and test results, and all gaps are explicitly listed.
3. The package is submitted through the security review board to the external certification laboratory.

## Risks / Notes

- Certification laboratory turnaround (historically six to nine months) and security review board cadence are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort; they dominate the program schedule but gate the certification outcome, not the engineering work in this strategy.
- Acknowledgment and triage of the submission by the external certification laboratory (following security review board sign-off) are externally controlled outcomes on the lab's own cadence, not engineering completion conditions; they are tracked as schedule risk. This epic's engineering completion point is submission of the package through the security review board.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): the compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab.

# Document the model serving stack FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites

## Description

Author the user-facing documentation stating the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, published through the Red Hat docs content process.

## Scope

Content outline:

- FIPS support posture of the model serving stack: which surfaces (KServe components, Platform Operator, serving data plane model-server runtimes) are supported on FIPS-enabled clusters and to what degree.
- Cluster prerequisites: FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster configuration and any installation or upgrade constraints.
- How to interpret the compliance status of the stack and the state of the certification submission.
- Placement of the new topics in the existing product documentation set for the model serving stack.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Published documentation states the FIPS support posture for the model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation.
2. The content is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior of the remediated serving stack, with the review recorded.
3. The documentation covers all remediated surfaces: KServe components, Platform Operator, and serving data plane model-server runtimes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. The epic's own priority is P0, derived from the strategy-level Critical priority per the docs-authoring priority exception, while the underlying HLR-4 remains P2.
